nodes.subject: electrical safety testing
nodes.object: Dielectric, insulation, earth-continuity, leakage-current and visual checks, with protection not dependent on one means alone.

support_spans.exact_quote: electrical products and installations must pass electrical safety tests.
Some types of electrical safety tests include: dielectric withstand test (also called a hipot test) insulation resistance test (IR test) earth continuity test leakage current test
A visual inspection seeks to identify damaged insulation, disconnected wires, incorrect installation, and any other visual issues.
No one means of protection should be totally necessary to the device's safety, so that the failure of one should not make the device immediately dangerous.

nodes.subject: melted magnetic-contact charger story

support_spans.exact_quote: it had obviously somehow broken enough to start melting itself and smoking almost right after I plugged it into an outlet
Both cables were broken before getting plugged in, and there was a 6 year time difference between them!

accepted_phrases: The melted-charger story concerns an already broken magnetic-contact charger for a different device that melted and smoked after plug-in. It supports immediately stopping use of damaged or smoking hardware, but it cannot identify a cause, failure rate, or safety ranking for the three phone-charger models.

nodes.subject: generic AC adapter safety design
nodes.object: Transformer isolation, jurisdiction-dependent certification and the need to match replacement voltage and current. These generic properties do not verify any captured charger model.

support_spans.exact_quote: Safety is ensured, as in the older linear circuit, because a transformer still provides galvanic isolation
must meet product safety regulations in many jurisdictions, usually requiring expensive certification
The replacement must match input and output voltages, match or exceed current capability

accepted_phrases: Generic AC-adapter evidence describes transformer isolation, jurisdiction-dependent safety certification, and matching replacement input, output and current capability. Those design and selection principles define evidence to seek but do not verify that any captured charger implements them correctly.

nodes.subject: fuse overcurrent protection
nodes.object: A conductor interrupting excessive current with application-specific current, voltage, breaking-capacity and response-time design. This does not prove a listed charger contains or correctly implements a suitable protection device.

support_spans.exact_quote: a fuse is an electrical safety device that operates to provide overcurrent protection of an electrical circuit.
Its essential component is a metal wire or strip that melts when too much current flows through it, thereby stopping or interrupting the current.
specific current and voltage ratings, breaking capacity, and response times, depending on the application.

accepted_phrases: A fuse interrupts excessive current by melting a conductor, but fuse designs have application-specific current, voltage, breaking-capacity and response-time properties. This generic mechanism does not prove that any listed charger contains or correctly implements suitable overcurrent protection.

nodes.subject: electrical overheating
nodes.object: Short circuit, overvoltage, poor heat dissipation, accidental fault, or wrong design or manufacture, with potential fire, explosion, injury and irreversible component damage.

support_spans.exact_quote: Overheating causes damage to the circuit components and can cause fire, explosion, and injury.
may be caused from any accidental fault of the circuit (such as short-circuit or spark-gap), or may be caused from a wrong design or manufacture

accepted_phrases: Electrical overheating can damage components and cause fire, explosion or injury, and possible causes include short circuit, overvoltage, poor heat dissipation, accidental fault, or wrong design or manufacture. These generic possibilities justify protection and stop-use checks but do not diagnose or rank the captured models.

nodes.subject: electronic product safety standards
nodes.object: Jurisdiction and product context. A generic standards list does not establish that an exact model and lot has a valid certification in the owner's jurisdiction.

support_spans.exact_quote: The manufacturers of electronic tools must take into account several standard for electronic safety to protect the health of humans and animals.

accepted_phrases: Electronic product makers must account for applicable safety standards, and the frozen standards evidence lists different jurisdictional systems. This establishes the need to bind a certification to the exact model and jurisdiction, not that any captured listing has done so.

nodes.subject: electrical safety testing
nodes.object: Dielectric withstand, insulation resistance, earth continuity, leakage-current tests and visual inspection. The captured listings provide no methods, thresholds, results or exact-model reports for these tests.

support_spans.exact_quote: electrical products and installations must pass electrical safety tests.
Some types of electrical safety tests include: dielectric withstand test (also called a hipot test) insulation resistance test (IR test) earth continuity test leakage current test
A visual inspection seeks to identify damaged insulation, disconnected wires, incorrect installation, and any other visual issues.
No one means of protection should be totally necessary to the device's safety, so that the failure of one should not make the device immediately dangerous.

accepted_phrases: Electrical safety testing can include dielectric withstand, insulation resistance, earth continuity and leakage-current tests, while visual inspection can identify damage or incorrect installation and multiple means of protection reduce single-point dependence. None of the three frozen listings supplies an exact-model report with methods, thresholds and results for these checks.

nodes.subject: USB-C capability boundary
nodes.object: Connector form from protocol, Power Delivery, cable capability and performance.

support_spans.exact_quote: The designation C refers only to the connector's physical configuration, or form factor, not to be confused with the connector's specific capabilities and performance
does not necessarily implement any USB transfer protocol, USB Power Delivery , or any of the Alternate Modes

accepted_phrases: USB-C identifies connector form rather than guaranteeing USB Power Delivery, cable capability or performance. Matching connector labels therefore do not establish the correct iPhone 13 cable, negotiated profile, or electrical safety of a charger.

nodes.subject: ratings brand and incident evidence
nodes.object: Small storefront ratings, price, brand, warranties and anonymous recommendations do not estimate failure prevalence or replace controlled exact-model testing. The different-device melted-charger story supports a damaged-hardware stop-use gate but cannot transfer its cause or prevalence to these models.

nodes.subject: model-bound electrical safety evidence
nodes.object: Bind applicable certification and electrical test results to the exact model, jurisdiction and product identity. Generic isolation, fuse, overheating and test-method evidence explains relevant mechanisms and checks; seller protection lists do not prove suitable implementation, thresholds or results.

nodes.subject: charger compatibility and preflight
nodes.object: Verify exact model, jurisdiction marking, certification record, iPhone 13 device-charger-cable profiles, seller identity and return path; account for two bricks and two USB-C-to-Lightning cables; inspect for damage, loose parts, discoloration, odor and abnormal heat; immediately isolate melting, smoking, sparking or repeatedly overheating hardware.
